itineraryStops.name: Pickup (Hongik University Station or Myeongdong Station)
itineraryStops.description:
Pickup is at one of two Seoul meeting points: **(1) Starbucks Hongik University Station Exit 8 (Mapo-gu)** at 07:30 — the Starbucks storefront sits immediately at the top of Exit 8; OR **(2) Myeongdong Station Exit 2 (Jung-gu)** at 08:00 — the NorthFace flagship store is the visible landmark next to the exit.

Both pickup points share the same air-conditioned coach, and Hongik passengers board first. Please be at your chosen point **5 minutes before the scheduled time**. This is a noticeably gentler start than the Seoraksan day trips, which leave at 06:00 — Gapyeong is close enough to Seoul that the coach can leave after the first subway trains have been running for two hours.

The guide distributes a printed Korean-English itinerary card at boarding and confirms the day's running order, the restroom stop, and the expected return times. From Myeongdong the coach heads northeast on the Seoul-Chuncheon Expressway for the roughly 1.5-hour drive to Gapyeong Wharf.
timeUsed: Arrive at your chosen pickup point 5 minutes before the scheduled time (~5 min)
Identify the AtoC Korea coach at the marked Starbucks / NorthFace frontage (~5 min)
Board in the pickup queue (~10 min)
Printed Korean-English itinerary card distributed at boarding
itineraryStops.whyOnRoute: Two pickup points cover Seoul's two main visitor clusters: the Hongik University area in Mapo-gu, which suits younger and short-stay travellers, and Myeongdong in Jung-gu, the legacy tourist district around the Lotte, Shilla and Westin hotels. Hongik first and Myeongdong second is the natural order for a northeast-bound run onto the Seoul-Chuncheon Expressway. The 07:30 start is late enough to be comfortable and early enough to put the coach on the Nami ferry at around 10:00, ahead of the independent day-trippers arriving by ITX train.

smartNotes.photo: Metasequoia avenue is the world-famous Winter Sonata shot — best in autumn (golden, late October-early November) or winter (snow). Riverside Lover's Ginkgo Tree Lane on the south side is quieter and equally photogenic. Albino peacock occasionally appears near Lover's Lane.
smartNotes.facilities: On-island restaurants serve Korean comfort food (hotteok, sweet potato latte, tteok-galbi). Sonata Cafe in a traditional hanok is the signature stop. Foreign-card-friendly ticket counter at Gapyeong Wharf — ticket machines do not accept foreign cards, ask at the counter.
smartNotes.tip: Best seasons: spring (April-May cherry blossoms), autumn (October golden ginkgo + red maple), winter (December-February snow-quiet paths reminiscent of Winter Sonata). Avoid the Sunday late-afternoon ferry queue.

itineraryStops.whyOnRoute: Nami opens the day because it is the one stop that rewards early light and punishes crowds. The half-moon island's metasequoia and ginkgo avenues are its signature, and they photograph best before midday when the independent travellers arriving by ITX train and the Gapyeong city tour bus fill the central lanes. Putting it first also means the ferry crossing happens in the morning calm rather than the afternoon wind, and it sets up the rest of the day to run inland and then home without doubling back.

convenience.restroom: Multiple on island and at Gapyeong Wharf
convenience.parking: Gapyeong Wharf 6,000 KRW small car / 10,000 KRW large vehicle

itineraryStops.description:
Nami Island opens the day's second chapter with a 5-minute ferry crossing from Gapyeong Wharf onto a half-moon-shaped river island in the Bukhan River. Approximately **460,000 m² (140,000 pyeong) and ~5 km in circumference**, Namiseom is named after **General Nami (Nam Yi, 1441-1468)**, a Joseon-era military commander executed at age 28 after being falsely accused of treason during the reign of King Yejong. 

The island originally became land only during floods; **in 1944 the Japanese colonial government built the Cheongpyeong Dam, raising the river level and making Nami a permanent island**. It found global fame **in 2002 as the filming location for KBS drama 'Winter Sonata'** starring Bae Yong-joon and Choi Ji-woo — the catalyst for the early 2000s Hallyu wave — and continues to draw about **3.3 million visitors annually (1.3 million foreign)**, making it Korea's most-visited single tourist destination after Seoul, Busan, and Jeju. 

Since **March 1, 2006** the island has branded itself as the self-declared **'Naminara Republic'** with its own flag, currency (Nami Tongbo coins), passport, and postal service — a tourism marketing concept rather than an actual political entity. 

The signature **Metasequoia tree-lined avenue** (Winter Sonata's iconic snowy lane), the **Riverside Lover's Ginkgo Tree Lane** on the south side, the **Korean Pine Road**, and the recycled-glass **Sequoia Bridge** made from soju bottles are all walkable in a relaxed two hours. On-island wildlife includes peacocks (including rare albinos), ostriches, wild rabbits, and squirrels. 

**The Naminara Republic VISA Fee (round-trip ferry included) is included in this tour price**.

visitBasics.hours: Ferry runs from 08:00, last boat in at 21:00 and last boat out at 21:05; every 10-20 min between 09:00 and 18:00 and every 30 min outside that, crossing about 5 minutes. Most on-island shops close by 18:00
visitBasics.admission: Naminara Republic visa fee, round-trip ferry included: Adult ₩19,000 — INCLUDED in this tour
visitBasics.walking: Easy — flat tree-lined paths; the half-perimeter walk is ~3 km, the full loop ~5 km. Bicycle and e-buggy rental available on the island for anyone who would rather not walk it.

itineraryStops.name: Lunch in Gapyeong (own expense)
itineraryStops.description:
The coach stops for an hour at a local restaurant in the Gapyeong Wharf area after Nami Island. Lunch is **not included** — you order and pay for what you want, which typically runs ₩10,000-15,000 per person.

This is dakgalbi country: the Chuncheon-Gapyeong corridor is the home of **dakgalbi**, sweet-spicy chicken stir-fried at the table with cabbage, sweet potato and rice cakes, usually finished by frying rice in the leftover sauce. **Makguksu** (cold buckwheat noodles) is the traditional partner dish. Vegetarian options are limited but bibimbap is normally available; tell the guide on the coach in the morning and they will call ahead.

Bring cash or card — most restaurants in the area take both, but small stalls near the wharf are often cash-only.
timeUsed: Coach parks and the guide walks the group to the restaurant (~5 min)
Order and eat (~45 min)
Pay individually and reassemble at the coach (~10 min)
itineraryStops.whyOnRoute: Lunch sits after Nami rather than before it for two reasons. First, it protects the morning: eating first would push the ferry crossing past midday and into the crowds. Second, the Gapyeong Wharf area is where the restaurants actually are — the Garden of Morning Calm is up a valley road with very little around it, and Petite France has only snack stalls on site. An hour here is the last reliable sit-down meal of the day.

smartNotes.photo: Spring (cherry blossoms April), summer (lush greens), autumn (foliage October-early November), and winter (lighting festival post-sunset) all photograph differently. The light tunnels at dusk during festival period are the iconic shot.
smartNotes.facilities: Food Garden serves Korean comfort food (soybean-paste stew, vegetable bibimbap, snow cheese tteokbokki). Good Morning Coffee in a hanok roasting house is the signature cafe. Restaurants close at 20:00.
smartNotes.tip: For the lighting festival (Dec 5 - Mar 15), the 17:00 arrival catches both daytime garden colours and the illumination ignition. Heavy snow February gives the most magical Frozen-movie scene.

itineraryStops.whyOnRoute: The Garden of Morning Calm is the day's middle chapter and its quietest one — 90 minutes is enough to walk the main loop past the Sunken Garden's Korean-peninsula flower beds and still sit down somewhere. It sits inland and uphill from the river, so it has to come after Nami and before the run home; visiting it in the early afternoon also catches the garden at its warmest, which matters from November through March when the valley holds the cold.

convenience.parking: Large free coach parking; coin lockers 1,500-2,000 KRW (500-KRW coins only)

itineraryStops.description:
About 30 minutes south of Nami Island, the Garden of Morning Calm is **Korea's signature private arboretum** — approximately **330,000 m²** of curated landscape with around **5,000 plant species**. Conceived in **1992** and opened to the public in **1996**, the garden was designed and personally cultivated by **Han Sang-kyung of Sahmyook University**, who at one point sold his house to fund the project; the name draws from Korea's longstanding nickname '**Land of the Morning Calm**' (Joseon). 

**Twenty themed sub-gardens** — including the **Sunken Garden shaped like the Korean peninsula**, the Hometown House Garden, the Bonsai Garden, the Moonlight Garden, the Sky Path, and the Garden of Eden — each carry their own visual identity and have served as filming sets for many K-dramas including **Moonlight Drawn by Clouds**. 

From early December to mid-March every winter, the garden hosts **Korea's first natural-environment lighting festival** with more than **200,000 environmentally-friendly LED bulbs** covering the grounds, transforming the garden after sunset into a winter wonderland. 

**The name 'Garden of Morning Calm'** comes from Indian poet Rabindranath Tagore, who in 1929 referred to Korea as 'the Land of Morning Calm.' Han Sang-kyung conceived the project in 1992 while serving as exchange professor in the United States, where he was inspired by world-class private gardens. 

**Han and his wife designed and personally labored on the garden**, and during periods of financial difficulty they sold their family home and lived in a small dwelling on the garden's property to continue construction. 

The garden first opened to the public on May 11, 1996, with 10 themed sections; today it has expanded to 20 themed sub-gardens across 330,000 m². **Admission is INCLUDED in this tour price**.

visitBasics.hours: Roughly 08:30 to sunset (commonly 08:30-19:00), last entry 18:00. During the winter Lighting Festival the garden stays open into the evening — hours change each season, and the guide confirms the day's closing time on the coach
visitBasics.walking: Moderate — extensive paths over rolling terrain through the themed sub-gardens; the main loop is mostly stroller-accessible

itineraryStops.name: Petite France
itineraryStops.description:
The day's compact final stop, Petite France is a French cultural theme village built into a hillside above Cheongpyeong Lake about 25 minutes from Nami Island. Opened in July 2008 by founder Han Hong-seop, the 16-building village is themed around 'flowers, stars, and the Little Prince' (Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's 1943 novel Le Petit Prince) and houses a Saint-Exupéry memorial hall, the Orgel House (a collection of antique music boxes featuring a 200-year-old centerpiece that still plays), a French housing exhibition, a marionette theater, and a gallery of le coq gaulois (Gallic rooster) sculptures and paintings. 

Drama fans visit primarily for the K-drama legacy: Petite France was the filming location for Beethoven Virus (2008), Personal Taste (2010), Secret Garden (2010), My Love from the Star (2013-2014), the 2025 hit Bon Appétit Your Majesty (Maison de Marie doubled as Im Yoon-ah's character's room), and the popular variety show Running Man. 

The adjacent Pinocchio & Da Vinci Italian Village offers a combo ticket option for visitors with extra time. The site has been selected for the 2026 Korea-France 140th Anniversary Commemorative Program. 

The village serves a dual function: French cultural theme village + the **Goseong Youth Training Center** that accommodates up to 200 visitors in 4-to-10-person rooms for educational stays. 

The site's most distinctive architectural feature is the **Traditional France Residence Gallery**: an entire 19th-century French farmhouse from middle-region France, dismantled and reassembled on-site using 200+-year-old wood, roof tiles, and bricks — joined entirely without nails using traditional French timber-frame mortise-and-tenon technique. 

Petite France is also **Korea's only Saint-Exupéry Foundation-licensed organization**, meaning every Little Prince motif on-site is officially authorized by the Foundation in France. 

The adjacent Pinocchio & Da Vinci Italian Village (separate ticket or combo at ₩19,500 adult) extends the day's European-village content by ~45 min if desired.

itineraryStops.whyOnRoute: Petite France closes the day because of where it is, not just what it is: the village sits on the Cheongpyeong lakeshore already pointing at Seoul, so an hour here costs no extra driving. It is also the day's smallest stop by some distance — sixteen buildings on a hillside, walkable in under an hour — which makes it the right note to end on after two hours on an island and ninety minutes in a garden. Fans of My Love from the Star, Secret Garden and Beethoven Virus will recognise it immediately.

visitBasics.hours: 09:00-18:00, last entry 17:00; closing time shifts with the season and on some evenings for scheduled night events
visitBasics.admission: Adult ₩12,000 — INCLUDED in this tour. The combined ticket with the adjacent Pinocchio & Da Vinci Italian Village (₩19,500 adult) is NOT included; the hour on this itinerary covers Petite France only
visitBasics.walking: Easy — a small village on a gentle hillside slope, comfortably walked in under an hour

smartNotes.photo: Pastel-colored timber-framed houses against the green mountain backdrop are the signature shots. The viewing deck at the top of the hill offers the best wide composition. K-drama scene-spotting is a guided activity for fans (Saint-Exupéry building = My Love from the Star pivotal scenes).
smartNotes.facilities: Snack stalls only — waffles, dumplings, fish-cake soup, coffee. Most visitors eat at adjacent Italian Village or in nearby Cheongpyeong town instead.
smartNotes.tip: Best paired with Nami Island and/or Garden of Morning Calm via the Gapyeong City Tour Bus for self-guided trips. Late-afternoon arrival lets you see daytime + early-evening illumination. Visitors expecting a large attraction often note the modest scale (1.5-2 hours typical) — manage expectations.

itineraryStops.name: Return to Seoul (Myeongdong or Hongik University Station)
itineraryStops.description:
Departure from Petite France is around 16:45 for the ~1.5-hour run back into Seoul on the Seoul-Chuncheon Expressway. Drop-offs are in reverse pickup order: **Myeongdong Station around 18:30**, then **Hongik University Station around 19:00**.

Both are subway interchanges, so onward connections are straightforward, and the timing leaves the evening open — you will be back well before Seoul's restaurants get busy. Friday evenings and Sunday returns can add 20-40 minutes of traffic on the approach to the city; the guide will give the coach's live estimate on the way in.
timeUsed: Depart Petite France (~16:45)
Motorway drive with one short comfort stop if needed (~1.5 hours)
Myeongdong Station drop-off (~18:30)
Hongik University Station drop-off (~19:00)
itineraryStops.whyOnRoute: Ending at Petite France rather than the Garden of Morning Calm is what makes the return short: the village is already on the Seoul side of Gapyeong, so the coach is pointed home the moment it leaves. Reversing the drop-off order means Myeongdong guests, who boarded last, get out first.

routePhases.description: Pickup at 07:30 Hongik / 08:00 Myeongdong, then a ~1.5-hour drive northeast to Gapyeong Wharf and the five-minute ferry across to Nami Island.
Flat tree-lined avenues, the Winter Sonata metasequoia lane, riverside benches and free-roaming ostriches and peacocks. Round-trip ferry and the Naminara Republic visa fee are included.
Lunch at a local restaurant in Gapyeong (own expense — dakgalbi country), then ~35 minutes inland and uphill to the Garden of Morning Calm for 90 minutes across its themed sub-gardens.
About forty-five minutes back down to the Cheongpyeong lakeshore for an hour at Petite France, then the ~1.5-hour run into Seoul — Myeongdong around 18:30, Hongik around 19:00.

routeShapeIntro.title: How this Seoul day moves
routeShapeIntro.subtitle: A 07:30 Hongik / 08:00 Myeongdong pickup and a ~1.5-hour drive northeast puts you on the Nami Island ferry before the day-trip crowds thicken. Lunch in Gapyeong town, then the loop turns inland and climbs to the Garden of Morning Calm, and finally drops back down to Petite France on the Cheongpyeong lakeshore — which sits on the way home, so the last stop costs you no backtracking. Back in Seoul around 18:30-19:00.

items.label: Nami first, before the crowds
items.detail: Gapyeong is only ~75 km from Seoul, so a 07:30 start reaches the wharf around 10:00 — ahead of the independent travellers arriving on the late-morning ITX trains, and with the low morning light still on the metasequoia avenue.

items.label: The gardens sit inland, the village sits on the way home
items.detail: The Garden of Morning Calm is up in Sang-myeon, ~35 minutes inland from the river; Petite France is back down on the Cheongpyeong lakeshore, already pointed at Seoul. Visiting them in that order means the last stop costs no backtracking.

items.label: Three admissions, one price
items.detail: Nami's ₩19,000 visa fee (round-trip ferry included), the Garden of Morning Calm's ₩11,000 and Petite France's ₩12,000 are all covered — about ₩42,000 of gate fees you don't queue for or pay again.

items.label: A shorter day than the Seoraksan routes
items.detail: Because nothing here is in Gangwon, the coach spends about three hours on the road instead of five. That is the whole reason this day feels relaxed where the Seoraksan itineraries feel long.

Camera or smartphone — the metasequoia avenue on Nami and the Sunken Garden viewpoint at Morning Calm are the two shots people come for.

practicalAccordionItems.title: Weather policy
content: Year-round operation.

Light rain: the tour runs as scheduled. All three stops hold up in rain — Nami's tree avenues and the Garden of Morning Calm are both genuinely good in wet weather, and Petite France has indoor exhibition rooms.
Heavy rain or storm: the Nami ferry can be suspended in severe weather. If that happens the guide extends the garden and Petite France stops and the Nami admission is refunded.
Snow: Gapyeong gets more snow than central Seoul. The coach carries winter tyres in season; heavy snowfall can add an hour to the return.
The itinerary order or timings may shift on the day for traffic, weather or venue operating hours — the guide confirms the day's plan on the coach.

practicalAccordionItems.title: Walking & terrain
practicalAccordionItems.preview: Easy to moderate — this route has no hiking and no stairs-heavy sections.
content: Easy to moderate — this route has no hiking and no stairs-heavy sections.
Nami Island: flat, paved, tree-lined avenues; ~3 km over 2 hours is the typical pace. Bicycles and e-buggies can be rented on the island at your own expense.
The Garden of Morning Calm: rolling terrain on mostly paved garden paths; the main loop is broadly stroller-accessible, though some themed sub-gardens sit up short slopes.
Petite France: a small hillside village, gentle slopes, under an hour at a relaxed pace.
Total walking across the day is roughly 5-6 km, spread over three stops with the coach in between. Comfortable shoes are enough — no hiking footwear needed.

practicalWeatherStatic._seasonalSummary: Seoul + Gangwon: temperate four-season climate. Seoraksan is 5-7°C cooler than Seoul year-round. Hot humid summers (Jun-Aug), crisp cold winters (Dec-Feb), with prime seasons in spring (April cherry blossoms) and autumn (October-November foliage).

seasonalVariations.description: Cherry blossom along the Bukhan River in early April, then the Garden of Morning Calm's spring festival with tens of thousands of tulips. Petite France's pastel buildings look their best against new green.

Nami's tree avenues give genuine shade and the island is noticeably cooler than Seoul. The garden is lush but hot and largely unshaded — carry water and sun cover. Expect afternoon showers in the July monsoon.

The strongest season on this route. Nami's metasequoia and ginkgo avenues turn through late October into mid-November, and the Garden of Morning Calm runs its autumn chrysanthemum display. Book early — this is peak demand.

The Garden of Morning Calm's Lighting Festival illuminates the grounds from early December to around mid-March, and the garden stays open into the evening during it. Nami under snow is the Winter Sonata image itself. Dress properly — the valleys are cold and the ferry deck is exposed.

bookingTrustItems.title: All admissions included
bookingTrustItems.body: Nami Island ferry (₩19,000) and Garden of Morning Calm (₩11,000) admissions are pre-paid into the tour price — no per-stop ticket queues. Seoraksan entrance is FREE (abolished May 2023). Total admission savings: ~₩30,000.

bookingTrustItems.title: Licensed English-speaking guide
bookingTrustItems.body: Korea Tourism Organization-licensed guide with English fluency; Chinese-speaking guide available on advance request. Guide narration covers Seoraksan's Silla-era temple history, Nami's Winter Sonata legacy, and Morning Calm's founder story.

bookingTrustItems.title: Transparent pricing
bookingTrustItems.body: No ginseng shops, no duty-free, no commissioned souvenir detours. Every minute of the 13-hour day is at an attraction or in transit — what you book is what you experience.

staticQuestions.question: Are all the admission fees really included?
staticQuestions.answer: Yes — the three gate fees on this route are all covered: Nami Island's ₩19,000 Naminara Republic visa fee (which includes the round-trip ferry), the Garden of Morning Calm's ₩11,000, and Petite France's ₩12,000. That is roughly ₩42,000 per adult you neither queue for nor pay again. Lunch is the main thing you pay for yourself.

staticQuestions.question: Is this the same as the Seoraksan tour that also visits Nami and Morning Calm?
staticQuestions.answer: No, and the difference is about three hours of driving. The Seoraksan day trip adds a national park in Gangwon-do, which means a 06:00 start, five hours on the road and a 13-hour day. This tour stays in Gapyeong: a 07:30 start, about three hours of driving, and Petite France in place of the mountain. Choose this one if you want the gardens and the island without the coach time.

staticQuestions.question: How much walking is there?
staticQuestions.answer: Roughly 5-6 km across the whole day, broken into three separate stops with the coach in between. There is no hiking, no summit and no long stair climbs. Nami is completely flat, the Garden of Morning Calm rolls gently, and Petite France is a small hillside village. Comfortable everyday shoes are enough.

staticQuestions.question: Is it suitable for young children or older travellers?
staticQuestions.answer: Yes, more so than most day trips from Seoul. Every stop is flat or gently sloping, the longest single drive is about 1.5 hours, and the day ends by 19:00. Nami rents bicycles and e-buggies if walking the island is too much, and the Garden of Morning Calm's main loop is broadly stroller-accessible. The one caveat is total day length — it is still 11 hours door to door.

staticQuestions.question: What is the Naminara Republic visa fee?
staticQuestions.answer: It is Nami Island's admission ticket, styled as a visa because the island declared itself the 'Naminara Republic' in 2006 as a cultural-tourism concept, complete with its own flag, stamps and immigration desk. Practically it is a ₩19,000 adult ticket that includes the five-minute ferry crossing both ways, and it is included in this tour.

staticQuestions.question: Can we visit the Italian Village next to Petite France?
staticQuestions.answer: Not within this itinerary. The Pinocchio & Da Vinci Italian Village sits on the hill directly behind Petite France and needs a combined ticket (₩19,500 adult) plus at least another hour. This tour includes Petite France only and allows an hour there. If the Italian Village matters to you, our private Gapyeong tour can build it in.

staticQuestions.question: What happens if it rains?
staticQuestions.answer: The tour runs. All three stops work in light rain — Nami's tree-lined avenues and the garden are both genuinely atmospheric wet, and Petite France has indoor exhibition rooms including the Saint-Exupéry hall and the Orgel House. The only real weather risk is a storm suspending the Nami ferry, in which case the guide extends the other two stops and the Nami admission is refunded.

staticQuestions.question: Is the Garden of Morning Calm Lighting Festival included?
staticQuestions.answer: The festival is not a separate ticket — it runs inside the garden, and your included admission covers it. But this is a daytime itinerary: we are at the garden in the early afternoon, so in the December-to-March festival season you will see the installations unlit rather than illuminated. If the lit garden is your priority, tell us and we will point you at an evening option instead.

staticQuestions.question: Which K-dramas were filmed at these stops?
staticQuestions.answer: Nami Island is the Winter Sonata (2002) location — the metasequoia avenue is the scene people come to stand in. Petite France's credits include Beethoven Virus (2008), Personal Taste (2010), Secret Garden (2010) and My Love from the Star (2013-14). The Garden of Morning Calm has also been used as a filming location, including for Moonlight Drawn by Clouds.

staticQuestions.question: What time do we get back to Seoul?
staticQuestions.answer: Myeongdong Station around 18:30 and Hongik University Station around 19:00. Both are subway interchanges. Friday evenings and Sunday returns can add 20-40 minutes on the approach into the city — the guide gives a live estimate on the way in. The timing is deliberately early enough to leave your evening free.

staticQuestions.question: Is lunch included?
staticQuestions.answer: No. The coach stops for an hour at a restaurant in the Gapyeong Wharf area and you order and pay for what you want, typically ₩10,000-15,000. This is the home region of dakgalbi — sweet-spicy chicken stir-fried at the table — usually eaten with makguksu noodles. Vegetarian choices are limited, so tell the guide in the morning and they will call ahead.

staticQuestions.question: Is there a guide, and in what language?
staticQuestions.answer: Yes — a licensed English-speaking guide travels with the coach for the whole day. A Chinese-speaking guide is available on request if you book at least three days ahead. The stops themselves are largely self-paced: the guide handles admission, timing, orientation and translation rather than delivering a continuous commentary.
